user_input: Who is Cedar Loop being built for?
reference: It is for one local hiking club, with a pilot limited to 40 club members.

user_input: What is the maximum size of the pilot group?
reference: The pilot is limited to 40 club members.

user_input: Which two user roles does the brief define?
reference: The roles are trip organizer and club member.

user_input: What details are recorded for a hike?
reference: A trip records its title, date and start time, trail name, meeting point, distance, elevation gain, difficulty, organizer notes, and participant limit.

user_input: How can a member respond to an upcoming trip?
reference: A member can RSVP yes or no, then change or withdraw the RSVP.

user_input: Who can see the trip roster?
reference: Only signed-in club members can see the roster.

user_input: Can anyone create an account through public self-registration?
reference: No. Organizers invite members, and there is no public self-registration.

user_input: Which sign-in method is included in the pilot?
reference: The pilot includes email and password sign-in.

user_input: Does the MVP include trail maps?
reference: No. Maps and external trail-data integrations are explicitly excluded.

user_input: Will the app send email or push notifications?
reference: No. Email and push notifications are not included in the pilot.

user_input: Can members pay for hikes in Cedar Loop?
reference: No. Payments are not included in the pilot.

user_input: How is the trip meeting point entered?
reference: The organizer enters the meeting point as text; the app does not use a map integration.

user_input: Does the app collect a member's home address?
reference: No. The brief says the app does not collect members' home addresses.

user_input: Which frontend framework is selected?
reference: The selected frontend is Next.js.

user_input: What backend framework and database are selected?
reference: The selected backend is FastAPI and the database is PostgreSQL.

user_input: Is the first release designed as several microservices?
reference: No. It is one web application with a managed PostgreSQL database, not a microservice system.

user_input: Which permissions apply to creating trips and changing RSVPs?
reference: Only organizers can create or edit trips. A member can update only their own RSVP.

user_input: What are the two pilot success measures?
reference: Organizers should create at least 10 trips, and at least 60% of invited members should RSVP within the first two weeks.

user_input: What happens when a hike is cancelled?
reference: A cancelled trip remains visible to signed-in members until its scheduled date and has a clear cancelled status.

user_input: How long should completed trip records be kept?
reference: Trip records should be retained for one year after the trip ends, then removed.

user_input: Must a member be online to change an RSVP?
reference: Yes. RSVP changes require a network connection; the app does not support offline changes.

user_input: What is the main mobile/network usability constraint?
reference: The app should work on a phone with intermittent cellular connectivity, but trip creation and RSVP changes still require a network connection.

user_input: Are organizer notes private to organizers?
reference: No. Organizer notes are visible to signed-in members and must not contain private medical information.

user_input: What is the expected uptime guarantee?
reference: The brief specifies no uptime guarantee.

user_input: Which payment processor did the club select?
reference: The brief does not select a payment processor; payments are outside the pilot scope.
